title: Foreign Electronic Components in Russian Weapons
description: These charts cover the foreign electronic components identified in Russian weapons. A “component” refers to a distinct part reference of an electronic product.
infos2: This page is a graphical representation of the data.
kpi1: Number of components manufactured outside Russia
kpi2: Country with the most components found in Russian weapons
kpi3: Company with the most components found in Russian weapons
kpi4: Weapon using the most components manufactured outside Russia
section2_title: Components by Weapon and Country of Origin

chart1.title: Foreign electronic components by equipment type
chart1.subtitle: Number of components identified in Russian weapons, by equipment type.

chart2.title: Components by weapon type
chart2.subtitle: Number of foreign electronic components identified in Russian weapons, by weapon type.

chart3.title: Components by country of origin (top 30)
chart3.subtitle: Number of foreign electronic components identified in Russian weapons, by country of origin.
chart3.help: The “country of origin” is the country where the company that makes the component is based. “Not identified” groups the components whose origin could not be established. Only the top 30 countries are shown.

chart4.title: Components by company of origin (top 30)
chart4.subtitle: Number of foreign electronic components identified in Russian weapons, by company of origin.
chart4.help: Each bar represents the company of origin of the components found in Russian weapons.

chart5.title: Components by weapon (top 30)
chart5.subtitle: Number of foreign electronic components identified in Russian weapons, by weapon.
chart5.help: A weapon is a specific model (for example Shahed-136 or Kh-101), whereas a weapon type groups several models (for example UAV or cruise missile). Only the 30 weapons with the most components are shown.

chart6.title: Components by weapon and country of origin (top 50)
chart6.subtitle: Number of foreign electronic components identified in Russian weapons, by weapon and then by country of origin.
chart6.help: Each bar represents a weapon, and its colored segments show the country of origin of its components. The total length is the number of components in that weapon. The detail of each segment is displayed on hover.

chart7.title: Foreign components in Russian weapons, by country of origin
chart7.subtitle: Number of components identified by country of origin, then by weapon (Shahed-136, Kh-101, Iskander-K…).
chart7.help: The blocks are nested: country of origin, then weapon. The area of each cell is proportional to the number of components identified. Zoom is enabled for the smallest cells.

chart8.title: Components by weapon type and equipment type
chart8.subtitle: Breakdown of the components identified in Russian weapons, by weapon type and equipment type.
chart8.help: The inner ring shows the equipment type, and the outer ring shows the weapon type within each category.
